info.title: Yumi Public Utilities
info.description: Standalone combined client view of three existing anonymous POST computations at the public Yumi site: wheel evidence, network-set evidence, and probe planning. This document describes exactly those three POST operations and does not create a new service, model, relay, persistence layer, or authentication boundary. Callers should submit public, non-secret inputs. The application routes do not require an account or authentication; the hosting provider may process ordinary request metadata. The existing runtime also keeps its descriptor GET, URL-encoded computation GET, and OPTIONS interfaces on these routes; those interfaces remain available but are deliberately outside this combined three-computation client view.

excludedButStillAvailable: Descriptor GET on each existing route
URL-encoded computation GET on each existing route
x-interface-scope.note: The excluded descriptor, encoded-GET, and OPTIONS interfaces remain part of the existing public runtime. Their omission here is a client-view scope choice, not a removal or replacement of those methods.

post.summary: Collect wheel evidence for explicit PyPI releases and tags
post.description: Existing anonymous POST computation. Accepts only application/json, including parameters such as charset. The streamed UTF-8 request body and any supplied Content-Length are capped at 65,536 bytes. The body must be a JSON object with exactly the releases and tags keys; request and item constraints are described by WheelEvidenceRequest. Up to two provider release requests are processed concurrently. Provider-reported results and provider failures remain explicit per release. The route does not download wheel files, retry requests, follow redirects, call a model, persist or log requests, or assess compatibility, installability, security, origin, digest verification, or artifact availability.

post.summary: Compare exact IPv4 and IPv6 address sets
post.description: Existing anonymous POST computation. Accepts only application/json, including parameters such as charset. The streamed UTF-8 request body and serialized input are capped at 16,384 bytes; each before and after array contains at most 64 CIDR strings, each at most 60 UTF-16 code units. The parsed object has exactly before and after keys. Input CIDRs are strict canonical-formatted address blocks with zero host bits; the exact grammar and refusal cases are described by NetworkCidr. The complete response, including producer metadata, is capped at 512 output CIDRs and 65,536 UTF-8 bytes; a limit failure rejects the whole result rather than truncating it. The route does not fetch externally, call a model, authenticate, persist or log requests, or assess reachability, routing, firewall, security policy, configuration, host usability, or access decisions.

post.summary: Plan minimum expected cost over a finite diagnostic model
post.description: Existing anonymous POST computation. Accepts only application/json, including parameters such as charset. The streamed UTF-8 request body and serialized model are capped at 65,536 bytes. The model has exactly hypotheses and probes keys; exact entry keys, array bounds, unique IDs, positive integer ranges, and complete outcomes mappings are described by ProbePlannerRequest. Text limits are runtime UTF-16 code-unit limits, which OpenAPI maxLength is not used to impersonate. The response reports exact safe-integer expected-cost ratios alongside decimal approximations and a recursively materialized policy. The route does not infer real-world truth, timing, probabilities, or costs; it does not call an external model, make outbound calls, persist or log models, or expose Yumi's private assistant, core, or memory.

NoSniff.description: The existing routes prevent content-type sniffing.

WheelCollectSuccess.description: Collected wheel evidence, including explicit per-release provider results.

WheelBadRequest.description: The POST request was invalid. The runtime returns INVALID_JSON for malformed JSON or invalid UTF-8, INVALID_REQUEST for a parsed request rejected by the wheel collector, or INVALID_CONTENT_LENGTH for an invalid Content-Length.

WheelPayloadTooLarge.description: The streamed POST body or its supplied Content-Length exceeds 65,536 bytes.

WheelUnsupportedMediaType.description: The POST Content-Type is absent or is not application/json.

WheelInternalError.description: An unexpected serialization or unclassified internal error occurred.

NetworkSuccess.description: Exact network-set comparison result with producer descriptor metadata.

NetworkBadRequest.description: The network-set POST request is invalid. The structured code and message identify invalid JSON/request shape or an invalid CIDR.

NetworkLimit.description: The serialized input exceeds 16,384 bytes, an input array exceeds 64 entries, the complete result exceeds 512 output CIDRs, or the complete result exceeds 65,536 UTF-8 bytes. The runtime never truncates a limited result.

error.message: The request exceeds an input limit.
The complete result exceeds an output limit.

NetworkUnsupportedMediaType.description: The POST Content-Type is absent or is not application/json. This existing route uses the INVALID_REQUEST structured error for this status.

NetworkInternalError.description: An unclassified internal or serialization error occurred.

error.message: The result could not be produced.

ProbeSuccess.description: Exact finite-model expected-cost result and its materialized policy.

ProbeBadRequest.description: The probe-plan POST request contains malformed JSON or a model rejected by the exact-key, type, length, uniqueness, completeness, or bounded-integer checks.

ProbePayloadTooLarge.description: The streamed POST body, its supplied Content-Length, or the decoded model exceeds 65,536 UTF-8 bytes.

ProbeUnsupportedMediaType.description: The POST Content-Type is absent or is not application/json.

ProbeInternalError.description: An unexpected serialization, arithmetic, or unclassified internal error occurred.

tags.description: Canonical lower-case uncompressed interpreter-ABI-platform triples; matching is literal intersection without compatibility expansion.

WheelEvidenceRequest.description: The implementation requires exactly these two top-level keys. Duplicate normalized project/version pairs are rejected even though that cross-item constraint is not expressible in this schema.

descriptor.description: Optional canonical service descriptor link observed on the deployed response.

enum: The request exceeds an input limit.
The complete result exceeds an output limit.
This HTTP method is not supported.
The result could not be produced.

NetworkError.description: The runtime emits the message paired with the code in ERROR_MESSAGES; the code/message relationship is fixed even though OpenAPI 3.0.3 cannot express that cross-property pairing in one enum schema.

NetworkSetRequest.description: Exactly two top-level keys are required. Empty arrays are valid. Unknown keys, non-array values, non-string entries, duplicate query parameters, malformed JSON, and unsupported forms are refused by the HTTP boundary.

NetworkCidr.description: Runtime grammar: strict IPv4 has exactly four decimal octets without leading zeroes, each 0..255; strict IPv6 has hexadecimal hextets and at most one case-insensitive :: compression marker expanding to eight hextets; prefixes use canonical decimal notation and stay within the family; host bits must be zero. Zones, dotted or IPv4-mapped IPv6, hostnames, URLs, and other forms are refused. The runtime also counts this bound in UTF-16 code units; valid accepted forms are ASCII, so this portable character bound does not replace the grammar.

equivalent.description: True exactly when all four family-specific added and removed address_count values are the decimal string 0.

NetworkSetResponse.description: Normalized contains minimal canonical CIDR decompositions. added is after minus before; removed is before minus after. IPv4 and IPv6 remain separate. Counts include every address, including network and broadcast addresses. The complete serialized UTF-8 response, including the producer descriptor, is at most 65,536 bytes and contains at most 512 CIDRs across all eight output lists.

NetworkOutputCidr.description: Canonical output CIDR. IPv4 is dotted decimal; IPv6 is lowercase hexadecimal with the longest zero run compressed, using the first-run tie break. The runtime's global output cap applies across lists, not independently to each list.

address_count.description: Exact decimal-string count of all addresses in this delta, including network and broadcast addresses.

address.description: The smallest address in the non-empty family-specific delta, formatted canonically.

enum: Each CIDR denotes an inclusive mathematical IPv4 or IPv6 address set.
Set comparison is performed separately for IPv4 and IPv6; duplicates, overlaps, and input order do not change a set.
Address counts include every address in the set, including network and broadcast addresses.

NetworkAssumptions.description: The runtime returns these three fixed assumptions in this order.

enum: This evidence does not assess firewall reachability, routing, security policy, or host usability.
This is an experimental prototype and makes no superiority, uniqueness, adoption, or security claim.

NetworkLimitations.description: The runtime returns these two fixed limitations in this order.

ProbePlannerRequest.description: The runtime accepts exactly these two top-level keys. It rejects unknown fields, duplicate hypothesis IDs, duplicate probe IDs, missing or unknown outcome keys, and any non-plain object record.

ProbeText.description: Runtime string bound is 1 through 64 UTF-16 code units. OpenAPI 3.0.3 maxLength is intentionally omitted because it is not a portable expression of that JavaScript UTF-16-unit rule.

ProbePositiveInteger.description: Runtime requires a safe integer from 1 through 1,000,000.

ProbeOutcomeMap.description: The runtime requires an ordinary object whose property set is exactly the unique hypothesis IDs from the same request: every hypothesis ID must occur once and no unknown ID may occur. OpenAPI 3.0.3 cannot express that cross-field exact-property-set constraint; additionalProperties here describes the value type, while the runtime rule is authoritative.

expectedCost.description: IEEE-754 decimal approximation of expectedCostNumerator / expectedCostDenominator.

ProbePlannerResponse.description: Exact integer numerator and denominator fields use safe integer arithmetic. Decimal expectedCost and nested probability fields are IEEE-754 approximations of exact integer ratios. Policy recursion is bounded by the finite supplied model; the runtime materializes at most 12 hypothesis levels.

enum: Hypothesis weights are treated as relative prior masses and normalized only for probabilities.
Expected cost is conditional on the supplied model.
Undistinguishable means identical complete outcome vectors across the supplied probes only.
Policy branch probabilities are conditional on the parent policy node.
Global undistinguishableGroups reports only non-singleton equivalence classes.
Weights and costs are positive integers from 1 through 1,000,000.
Hypothesis IDs, probe IDs, and outcome strings contain 1 through 64 UTF-16 code units.
Expected-cost numerators and denominators use exact safe integer arithmetic.
Decimal expectedCost and probability fields are IEEE-754 approximations of adjacent exact integer ratios.

ProbeAssumptions.description: The runtime returns these ten fixed assumptions in this order.

ProbeProbability.description: Runtime probability is strictly greater than zero and at most one; exact numerator and denominator fields accompany it.

ProbeHypothesisIds.description: IDs preserve the supplied hypothesis order and are unique because the request rejects duplicates.
